content_md:
Feel like a more resalinating aspect of Blygger as a publishing medium comes from its lack of likes as an engagement metric and a real focus on replies.

I notice more of an urge to exposit my thoughts in a way that doesn’t rely on densely shared context or memeplexes for decompression, instead we have the ambient blygosphere. Ideas truly live and die off their own ontological rigor here, which feels exciting to stress-test my own skills as a writer.
